note: Platform lore: what a platform says (and what we only suspect). Floor, not the whole picture: rules change ad hoc and part of them are unwritten. `OPEN` means unresolved: policy.py check lists it before publishing. Copy to <world>/platform_rules.json with `policy.py init`.

rules.statement: Generic or repetitive content (renamed from 'repetitious content' to 'inauthentic content', 2025-07-15) includes content that looks like it's made with a template.
rules.quote: Generic or repetitive content includes content that looks like it's made with a template
rules.note: Our guard: distinct check on the novelty keys; vary mechanism, outcome, set and title pattern across episodes.

rules.statement: Characters put in the same situation over and over with the same outcome are repetitive content.
rules.quote: Videos where characters are put in the same situation over and over again with the same outcome
rules.note: Maps to novelty keys premise, mechanism+outcome.

rules.statement: Similar content with minimal variation across videos is repetitive content.
rules.quote: Similar or repetitive content with low educational value, commentary, narratives, or minimal variation across videos
rules.note: Maps to the whole novelty-key set: a run of episodes sharing most keys is minimal variation.

rules.statement: A series following a set of characters across episodes is listed as allowed. Our reading, not the page's: each video needs its own storyline, focus or concept.
rules.quote: Similar content, like a series following a set of characters across episodes
rules.note: The distinct-storyline condition is the research file's reading (3P), not a quoted line. Enforced by the distinct check.

rules.statement: How stylised, reusable animation (one rig, many episodes) is judged under the repetitive-content rule.
rules.note: The page does not mention animation. Unresolved; resolve with an experiment or a platform answer, or acknowledge in world.brief policy.acks.

rules.statement: How synthetic or cloned voices are treated: monetisation, and whether any disclosure applies.
rules.note: The page does not mention synthetic voice. Unresolved; check YouTube's other policy pages for a disclosure rule before publishing and record the finding here.

rules.statement: Dozens of near-identical templated uploads a day risk demonetisation of the whole channel.
rules.note: Third-party reading of the policy; the cadence in world.brief is the lever.

rules.statement: A first frame or title that does not match the content can be treated as deceptive practice.
rules.note: Stated in research/shorts_hooks.md section 5 without a fetched quote: not re-read for this seed. Re-fetch before relying on it.

rules.statement: Enforcement details (thresholds, how many near-duplicates trip the rule, human or automatic review) are not published.
rules.note: Standing unknown: treat the written policy as a floor. Track by experiments and by our own channel's Studio notices.
